;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**[[Ecuador]]ian drug trafficker and [[FARC dissidents|FARC dissident]] [[Walter Arizala]] is killed in a joint police and military operation near [[Tumaco]]. Arízala was wanted for the murder of two Ecuadorian journalists earlier in the year. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-46657846 (BBC)] 

;Business and economy
*[[Gatwick Airport drone incident]]
**Two people are arrested by [[Sussex Police]] and charged with "criminal use of drones".  [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/dec/22/gatwick-drone-arrests-two-people-held-over-disruption-of-airport (''The Guardian'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*At least 23 people are killed and 14 injured in [[Dang Deukhuri District]], [[Nepal]], when a bus carrying students and their teachers returning from a botanical trip runs off a road and plunges 700 meters into a ravine. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-46658873 (BBC)]
*At least 13 miners, eleven [[Polish people|Poles]] and two [[Czechs]], are killed and 10 injured in a [[methane]] explosion in a coal mine in [[Karvina]], [[Czech Republic]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-46644793 (BBC)]
*Five people are killed and dozens injured when a train slams into a bus carrying school students in [[Niš]], [[Serbia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-46653202 (BBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[Criminal justice reform in the United States]]
**U.S. President [[Donald Trump]] signs the [[First Step Act]], a bipartisan prison and sentencing reform bill, into law. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2018/dec/21/trump-prison-reform-first-step-act-signed-law (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Carlos Ghosn]], formerly the chairman of [[Nissan]], is arrested again on suspicion of shifting personal losses to the company. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/carlos-ghosn-re-arrested-on-suspicion-of-shifting-personal-losses-to-nissan-11545360451 (''Wall Street Journal'')]
*A [[Canadians|Canadian]] judge denies former [[Guantanamo Bay detention camp|Guantanamo Bay]] detainee [[Omar Khadr]]'s request for relaxed bail conditions and a [[Canadian passport]]. [https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/nation/canadian-judge-denies-omar-khadr-eased-bail-conditions/ (''Seattle Times'')] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/edmonton-judge-khadr-request-bail-conditions-1.4955568 (CBC)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 United States federal budget]]
**The U.S. Congress adjourns for the night before reaching a new budget agreement, starting [[United States federal government shutdown of 2018–19|a partial federal government shutdown]] that began the next day at 12:00 a.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]] (05:00 [[Coordinated Universal Time|UTC]]). [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/bill-fund-border-wall-teeters-edge-senate-n950831 (NBC News)]
*A [[motion of no confidence]] is passed by the [[National Assembly (Guyana)|National Assembly]] of [[Guyana]] with a vote of 33–32, triggering early elections scheduled for 2019. [https://www.stlucianewsonline.com/guyana-ppp-wins-no-confidence-motion-afc-mp-persaud-sides-with-opposition/ (''St. Lucia News Online'')]

;Science and technology
*[[Largest known prime number]]
**The [[Great Internet Mersenne Prime Search]] announces the discovery of a new [[Mersenne prime]], 2<sup>82,589,933</sup>-1. It has 24,862,048 decimal digits, which surpasses the previous record by over 1.5 million digits.  [https://www.npr.org/2018/12/21/679207604/the-world-has-a-new-largest-known-prime-number (NPR)]
